      "unit": "F034:F043",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": ["term.state"],
        "statement": "The purposes of chapter 106 are (1) to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act); and (2) to accomplish those goals through strengthening community capabilities for planning and coordinating broad assistance responsive to local needs; organizing services related to low-income family and individual needs to have measurable and potentially major impact on causes of poverty and help achieve self-sufficiency; greater use of innovative and effective community-based approaches to attacking poverty and community breakdown causes and effects; maximum participation of residents of low-income communities and members of groups served by block grant assisted programs to empower them to respond to unique community problems and needs; and broadening the resource base to secure a more active role in service provision for private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations as well as individual citizens, business, labor, and professional groups.",

unit_attributes.statement: The purposes of chapter 106 are (1) to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act); and (2) to accomplish those goals through strengthening community capabilities for planning and coordinating broad assistance responsive to local needs; organizing services related to low-income family and individual needs to have measurable and potentially major impact on causes of poverty and help achieve self-sufficiency; greater use of innovative and effective community-based approaches to attacking poverty and community breakdown causes and effects; maximum participation of residents of low-income communities and members of groups served by block grant assisted programs to empower them to respond to unique community problems and needs; and broadening the resource base to secure a more active role in service provision for private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations as well as individual citizens, business, labor, and professional groups.

The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall take steps, consistent with law, to allow funds available through the Community Services Block Grant program to be used by grantees and eligible entities to provide emergency learning scholarships to disadvantaged families for use by any child without access to in-person learning, which scholarships may be used for tuition and fees for a private or parochial school; homeschool, microschool, or learning-pod costs; special education and related services, including therapies; or tutoring or remedial education.

unit_attributes.actor_quote: The Secretary of Health and Human Services

unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in Executive Order 13969 shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof, or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
Executive Order 13969 shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

Executive Order 13969 is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

In chapter 106, "eligible entity" means an entity that is an eligible entity described in paragraph (1) (as in effect on the day before October 27, 1998) as of the day before October 27, 1998, or is designated by the process described in section 9909 of title 42 (including an organization serving migrant or seasonal farmworkers that is so described or designated), and that has a tripartite board or other mechanism described in subsection (a) or (b), as appropriate, of section 9910 of title 42.
In chapter 106, the term "family literacy services" has the meaning given the term in section 9832 of title 42.

In chapter 106, the term "poverty line" means the official poverty line defined by the Office of Management and Budget based on the most recent data available from the Bureau of the Census; the Secretary shall revise the poverty line annually (or at any shorter interval determined feasible and desirable), which line shall be used as an eligibility criterion in the community services block grant program, accomplished by multiplying the official poverty line by the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the interval immediately preceding the revision.

Whenever a State determines that it serves the objectives of the block grant program established under chapter 106, the State may revise the poverty line to not to exceed 125 percent of the official poverty line otherwise applicable under paragraph (2) of section 9902.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Whenever a State determines that it serves the objectives of the block grant program established under this chapter

unit_attributes.statement: In chapter 106, the term "private, nonprofit organization" includes a religious organization, to which the provisions of section 9920 of title 42 shall apply.
In chapter 106, the term "Secretary" means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

In chapter 106, the term "State" means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, the United States Virgin Islands, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary for each of fiscal years 1999 through 2003 to carry out the provisions of chapter 106 (other than sections 9922 and 9923 of title 42).
unit_attributes.scope_text: for each of fiscal years 1999 through 2003

unit_attributes.statement: Of the amounts appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for each fiscal year, the Secretary shall reserve 1/2 of 1 percent for carrying out section 9905 of title 42 (relating to payments for territories).

Of the amounts appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for each fiscal year, the Secretary shall reserve 1 1/2 percent for activities authorized in sections 9913 through 9918 of title 42, of which not less than 1/2 of the amount reserved under paragraph (2) shall be distributed directly to eligible entities, organizations, or associations described in section 9913(c)(2) of title 42 for the purpose of carrying out activities described in section 9913(c) of title 42.

Of the amounts appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for each fiscal year, of the 1 1/2 percent reserved under paragraph (2) for activities authorized in sections 9913 through 9918, 1/2 of the remainder of the amount reserved shall be used by the Secretary to carry out evaluation and to assist States in carrying out corrective action activities and monitoring (to correct programmatic deficiencies of eligible entities), as described in sections 9914(c) and 9913 of title 42.

Of the amounts appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for each fiscal year, the Secretary shall reserve 9 percent for carrying out section 9921 of title 42 (relating to discretionary activities) and section 9917(b)(2) of title 42.
The Secretary is authorized to establish a community services block grant program and make grants through the program to States to ameliorate the causes of poverty in communities within the States.

The Secretary shall apportion the amount reserved under section 9903(b)(1) of title 42 for each fiscal year on the basis of need among Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

Each jurisdiction to which subsection (a) applies (Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands) may receive a grant under section 9905 of title 42 for the amount apportioned under subsection (a) on submitting to the Secretary, and obtaining approval of, an application containing provisions describing the programs for which assistance is sought under section 9905, prepared in accordance with and containing the information described in section 9908 of title 42.
unit_attributes.actor: Each jurisdiction to which subsection (a) applies

unit_attributes.scope_text: on submitting to the Secretary, and obtaining approval of, an application, containing provisions that describe the programs for which assistance is sought under this section, that is prepared in accordance with, and contains the information described in, section 9908 of this title

unit_attributes.statement: The Secretary shall, from the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for each fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) of title 42, allot to each State (subject to section 9911 of title 42) an amount bearing the same ratio to such remaining amount as the amount received by the State for fiscal year 1981 under section 2808 of title 42 bore to the total amount received by all States for fiscal year 1981 under such section, except that no State shall receive less than 1/4 of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) for such fiscal year, and except as provided in subsection (b) of section 9906.
unit_attributes.scope_text: for each fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) of this title

unit_attributes.statement: Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3) of section 9906(b), if the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of title 42 for a fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) exceeds $345,000,000, the Secretary shall allot to each State not less than 1/2 of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) for such fiscal year.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), if the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of this title for a fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) of this title exceeds $345,000,000

unit_attributes.statement: Paragraph (1) of section 9906(b) shall not apply with respect to a fiscal year if the amount allotted under subsection (a) to any State for that year is less than the amount allotted under section 9903(a)(1) of title 42 (as in effect on September 30, 1989) to such State for fiscal year 1990.

unit_attributes.statement: The amount allotted under section 9906(b)(1) to a State for a fiscal year shall be reduced, if necessary, so that the aggregate amount allotted to such State under such paragraph and subsection (a) does not exceed 140 percent of the aggregate amount allotted to such State under the corresponding provisions of chapter 106 for the preceding fiscal year.
